{"caption":"Diagram of a persistent wiki recording proposals and evidence that inform an evolving active skill.","description":"The diagram has two main columns. On the left, a small lightbulb-and-open-book icon sits above “Persistent Wiki Layer (wiki/)”, suggesting stored knowledge. Three gray file panels are shown. The top panel, “skill-impact.md”, contains a proposal history: Iteration 0 creates “goal-directed-action” and is marked in a red “REJECTED” label; a diff headed “@@ -0,0 +1,128 @@” shows removal of “/dev/null” and additions “goal-directed-action/SKILL.md”, “# Goal-Directed Action”, and an ellipsis. Iteration 1 creates “break-repetition-loop” and Iteration 4 updates it; both are marked with green “ACCEPTED” labels, with ellipses indicating omitted content. A red arrow from the rejected proposal points right into PURPOSE.md and is labeled “Prior Rejection History Explains Skill Rationale”. Green connectors from the accepted proposal entries point right into the active skill area, labeled “Accepted Proposed Skill Update”.

The middle gray panel, “logs.md”, records: Iteration 0, creation of “take-examine-move-loop.md” (train: 00, 02) and rejection of skill “goal-directed-action” (val score = 0.72); Iteration 1, “Errors Re-occurring” (train: 01, 02), “Use-Examine Loop (NEW) in train: 30, 31”, fresh evidence appended to “take-examine-move-loop.md”, and acceptance of skill “break-repetition-loop” (val score = 0.78), followed by an ellipsis. A blue curved arrow points left into logs.md from the patterns area; its label reads “Evolution Log Chronologically Records Patterns and Decisions”.

The lower gray panel, “patterns”, contains two documented patterns. “take-examine-move-loop.md” says the agent takes an item, examines it, puts it back, and repeats. Its evidence reads: Iter 0, train 00 and 02; Iter 1, train 01; Iter 2–4, train 02 persists, while 00/01 show recovery from loops. “multi-operation-loop.md” says cycles of actions on the same item occur without checking completion. Its evidence reads: Iter 2, train 22 and 24; Iter 3–4, train 24 persists. An orange connector points from the pattern records toward rules in SKILL.md, labeled “Documented Patterns Motivate the Skill Update Proposals at Iterations 1 and 4”.

On the right, a folder icon sits above “Active Skill Layer (skills/)”. A large pale-green group labeled “break-repetition-loop” contains PURPOSE.md and SKILL.md. PURPOSE.md says the skill was created as “break-repetition-loop”; a previous attempt, “goal-directed-action”, was rejected for being too abstract, and this version is more concise and uses concrete action patterns. SKILL.md says: “Trigger: Apply the skill whenever the agent is about to repeat an action.” Its first rule is “Never Return an Item to Its Origin Location”, contrasting a failing example, “take clock from desk -> examine -> move clock to desk”, with a successful one, “take clock -> go to shelf -> move clock to shelf”. A second rule says agents that do take items and perform operations often get stuck repeating the same operation, and specifies “Each Operation Type ONCE Per Item”. The anti-pattern is “Take -> Operate -> Move -> Take (INFINITE CYCLE)”; the fix is to complete “take -> operate -> move” once and not repeat. Below the group is a separate pale-green “other-skill” bar with an ellipsis. The proposal-status pills are the only explicit rejected/accepted marks; no check or cross symbols are shown.","figure_type":"diagram","chart_values":[]}
